**Required Info:**

    Operating System: Ubuntu22.04

    Computer: X86_64

    ROS2 Version:ros-humble（**humble_main branch**）

    Version or commit hash: humble_main:latest

**Steps to reproduce issue**

Simulation Environment: Turtlebot3 + gazebo  +  nav2_smac_planner (Hybrid a star)

**Question**

I am using humble_main branch, nav2_smac_planner, I believe this route is divided into two segments: one segment is the forward extension, and the second segment is generated by the analytic_expansion. My questions are: 
         1)  The endpoint of the forward extension and the starting point of the analytic_expansion should be coincide, rather than overlap? 
         2) If question1) is right, I want to avoid any backward motion caused by 1）. Can this be achieved through a smoothing plugin?

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/754d3a47-6bc3-466c-834b-fc28e781f05b)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88c0b170-2fa5-4bcd-8103-e374e1f46f37)


Does this happen on Humble or Jazzy branch? I'm wondering if some recent work introduced a regression https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/4127. That work is not backported to Humble / Jazzy so if you don't see it there, that would point to an issue with this PR which touches the part of the code that could cause something like this. 

This should absolutely not be happening with the only exception: If your robot's turning radius is too large to make a turn, it might actually choose to go backwards at a turn, to go forward again from another angle in order to make the turn. Think of it as a 3-point turn maneuver. Please verify that this is not the case first before we go further (but from these 2 images it looks like its at the junction with the analytic expansions, so I don't think that's the case - it looks like a regression. You'd see this behavior elsewhere than just the switch to the analytic expansions if it were a turning radius related issue). 

FYI @stevedanomodolor I think this points out a potential issue with your PR

## Issue 1: Refine Path Issue (Tentatively Completed)

I'm thinking @stevedanomodolor's PR solves the issue @wang-fire  brought up in https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5188 and https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5192#issuecomment-2911274182. @wang-fire can you review, test locally, and let us know if that resolves this element so you can use `humble_main` again? I believe that it should and an important incremental fix.

Edit: I merged https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/5198 after @stevedanomodolor said he was able to test briefly and couldn't reproduce it but would appreciate your final 👍 @wang-fire. I suspect this can be called _COMPLETED_ now

## Issue 2: Reeds-Shepp Single-Point Oddity (In Progress)

With respect to the single point issue in the original ticket, I can reproduce that on Jazzy myself when using the default parameters in the [Docs](https://docs.nav2.org/configuration/packages/smac/configuring-smac-hybrid.html) with the change of using the Reeds-Shepp model rather than Dubins (no issue with dubins). So, I don't think its just parameterizations. 

Update with development results 5:29pm PST: 

I'll spare you the convoluted details about how I got here, but I was able to log inside of the analytic expansion the directional turns that the reeds-shepp paths themselves generated and found that I was correct that it is the Reeds-Shepp paths legit have the extra backup-and-then-move-forward behavior. While most of the time I see it happen due to the turning radius refinement stage, I can also see it normally happen in the raw Reeds-Shepp path that is generated by OMPL as the shortest possible path. That is the legit, shortest path using Reeds-Shepp curves so that is technically correct behavior. 

Thus, this isn't strictly speaking a bug, this is intended behavior to have the shortest minimum turning radius path to the goal pose and orientation. Though, I fully ACK that this can be annoying or look like a bug. Possible suggestions (**any other suggestions?**):
- Do nothing, this is actually drivable and correct
- Limit the analytic expansion curve to be facing in the same direction of motion as the expansion it represents is in (i.e. forward primitive must start with forward, reverse primitive must start with reversing). While that would completely eliminate the possibility of a path like this, that would open up an edge case possibly in confined settings where this is strictly necessary to be able to find an exact route to the goal. I suppose it could be parameterized, however it doesn't prevent other reversing-type plans > 1 point long. 
- We could add in an additional refinement heuristic that prefers solutions with less directional changes, even if at the cost of a longer path and/or path closer to potential obstacles. That could eliminate some of them, but wouldn't make it impossible to happen
- We could add a constraint on the refinements so that it should not add any more directional changes than the original solution provides. If it does, then we consider it less optimal and don't consider it further, even if its shorter or in lower cost space. 

I think the last one is the best in my opinion.  I have a prototype in https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/5207 to test. If the shortest path by the turning radius really does involve doing that, maybe we should let it. However, if it happens due to refinements for cost weighting / increasing turning radius, perhaps we should prefer sticking with the original value (or another turning value that's not as extreme) which doesn't increase that count. That makes it still possible to happen, but only if its natural for it to happen and not due to later refinement. I'm finding that most of the time this happens is due to the refinement stage, so this would remove some big percentage of them. I also married it with a check to see if there's a refinement that is less than the original cost (but might be larger than some other refined cost) and uses less segments to use. If its better than original and less directional segments, I think that is the preferable direction over slightly shorter but having 2x direction changes. 

What does everyone think?

## Issue 1: Refine Path Issue (Tentatively Completed)

I'm thinking @stevedanomodolor's PR solves the issue @wang-fire  brought up in https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5188 and https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/5192#issuecomment-2911274182. @wang-fire can you review, test locally, and let us know if that resolves this element so you can use `humble_main` again? I believe that it should and an important incremental fix.

Edit: I merged https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/5198 after @stevedanomodolor said he was able to test briefly and couldn't reproduce it but would appreciate your final 👍 @wang-fire. I suspect this can be called _COMPLETED_ now

## Issue 2: Reeds-Shepp Single-Point Oddity (In Progress)

With respect to the single point issue in the original ticket, I can reproduce that on Jazzy myself when using the default parameters in the [Docs](https://docs.nav2.org/configuration/packages/smac/configuring-smac-hybrid.html) with the change of using the Reeds-Shepp model rather than Dubins (no issue with dubins). So, I don't think its just parameterizations. 

Update with development results 5:29pm PST: 

I'll spare you the convoluted details about how I got here, but I was able to log inside of the analytic expansion the directional turns that the reeds-shepp paths themselves generated and found that I was correct that it is the Reeds-Shepp paths legit have the extra backup-and-then-move-forward behavior. While most of the time I see it happen due to the turning radius refinement stage, I can also see it normally happen in the raw Reeds-Shepp path that is generated by OMPL as the shortest possible path. That is the legit, shortest path using Reeds-Shepp curves so that is technically correct behavior. 

Thus, this isn't strictly speaking a bug, this is intended behavior to have the shortest minimum turning radius path to the goal pose and orientation. Though, I fully ACK that this can be annoying or look like a bug. Possible suggestions (**any other suggestions?**):
- Do nothing, this is actually drivable and correct
- Limit the analytic expansion curve to be facing in the same direction of motion as the expansion it represents is in (i.e. forward primitive must start with forward, reverse primitive must start with reversing). While that would completely eliminate the possibility of a path like this, that would open up an edge case possibly in confined settings where this is strictly necessary to be able to find an exact route to the goal. I suppose it could be parameterized, however it doesn't prevent other reversing-type plans > 1 point long. 
- We could add in an additional refinement heuristic that prefers solutions with less directional changes, even if at the cost of a longer path and/or path closer to potential obstacles. That could eliminate some of them, but wouldn't make it impossible to happen
- We could add a constraint on the refinements so that it should not add any more directional changes than the original solution provides. If it does, then we consider it less optimal and don't consider it further, even if its shorter or in lower cost space. 

I think the last one is the best in my opinion.  I have a prototype in https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/pull/5207 to test. If the shortest path by the turning radius really does involve doing that, maybe we should let it. However, if it happens due to refinements for cost weighting / increasing turning radius, perhaps we should prefer sticking with the original value (or another turning value that's not as extreme) which doesn't increase that count. That makes it still possible to happen, but only if its natural for it to happen and not due to later refinement. I'm finding that most of the time this happens is due to the refinement stage, so this would remove some big percentage of them. I also married it with a check to see if there's a refinement that is less than the original cost (but might be larger than some other refined cost) and uses less segments to use. If its better than original and less directional segments, I think that is the preferable direction over slightly shorter but having 2x direction changes. 

What does everyone think?

Specifically, a planner (I use the lattice one, humble_main branch) can sometimes generate an incorrect x (and possibly y) value in the goal pose, resulting in an entirely incorrect path to the another, not target, position. I tested reverting commit https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/commit/f5543c39aba5d3302208bc6e9696e7cbd41de8c9, and that resolved the problem. But I have no idea how is it possible.
